producer_report.summary: Two fixes. (1) The email allow-list scan now runs inside the producer loop. After each producer report, `Athena::working_diff_scan` runs the same rule and `[personal_data]` allow-list as admission on the work tree's diff against its base. It numbers added lines only, so an address already in the base is not blamed. A finding goes back through the existing single send-back as `<path>:<line> adds an email address outside the allow-list`, with a brief section that names each file and line. If the address is still there once the send-back is spent, the run fails with `admission refused the change: README.md:3 adds ...` and no candidate is built. Admission keeps its own scan as a backstop. One line was added to the producer prompt. Root cause 1: no in-loop scan, so the producer learned of an address only when the finished candidate was refused, and the refusal named no line. (2) Introspection now matches earlier cases on the admission refusal. `narrow_cases` lists first the cases whose job's outcome has the same admission rule (`admission::refusal_keys`, keyed on the rule's fixed words, not the file), then the class/category matches, capped at CASE_CAP. `Records.job_reasons` is filled from outcome files and overlaid from git records. A job with the same refusal but no recorded introspection is named in a flag on the new record. Root cause 2: `narrow_cases` matched only on class_of_work and category and never read an outcome's refusal reason, and `apply_answer` drops every case not passed in and in the chosen class. A model shown no earlier case picks `new`, so the record gets new_class=true and empty earlier_cases. I could not confirm which condition produced the 4nff record, because records/ is absent. The code, comments and CHANGELOG name the candidates: a different class or category, five or more newer cases in the bucket, no recorded introspection for the earlier jobs, or outcomes held in git but not on disk. Tests: 3 content tests, 2 refusal_keys tests, 3 producer-loop tests, 1 introspect test, 1 cli narrow_cases test, 1 prompt test.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-core: a new test gives the producer a working diff adding a disallowed email address on a known line of a known file and asserts the producer's run fails with a message naming that file and line; the test fails on the base code and passes with the change.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-core _working_diff` passes. `a_disallowed_email_in_the_producers_working_diff_is_sent_back_then_fails_the_run` has the fake producer write README.md with an address on line 3. It asserts: two producer turns; the second brief and a 'producer   sent back:' UI line both contain 'README.md:3 adds an email address outside the allow-list'; the job closes Failed with a reason starting 'admission refused the change: ' that contains README.md:3 and not the address; no 'candidate' UI line; no verification. On base there is no in-loop scan, so the ':3', no-send-back and no-candidate-line assertions would fail. I did not run it on the base.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-core: a test with an allow-listed address (or none) in the working diff asserts the producer run is not failed by the new scan.
criteria_check.evidence: `an_allow_listed_address_in_the_producers_working_diff_does_not_fail_the_producer_run` passes. For a no-reply example.com address and for no address, it asserts one producer turn, no 'sent back' line, a 'candidate' line, state Landed and no allow-list text in the reason. The send-back-then-fixed test also lands.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-core: a new introspect test builds records where two earlier jobs' outcomes record 'adds an email address outside the allow-list' and asserts the narrowed earlier-case list for a new event with that refusal includes both, and that the resulting introspection record has non-empty earlier_cases and is not marked new_class; it fails on the base code.
criteria_check.evidence: `introspect::tests::earlier_cases_match_on_the_admission_refusal_reason` passes. Two outcome files are written to a tempdir and read by `read_records` into `job_reasons`; two more reasons come in through `add_job_reasons`. Six newer unrelated cases fill the cap. The narrowed list has the three refusal cases first and has length 5. An event with a different admission rule pulls none of them. `unrecorded_matches` names the job with no case. `apply_answer` with the base-style list drops both cited ids into dropped_ids and leaves earlier_cases empty. With the narrowed list it keeps both, with no dropped ids, status Recorded and new_class false. On base the test does not compile, because `job_reasons` and `Event.reason` do not exist.

criteria_check.criterion: The change refuses more producer runs than before by design: expected 5% of newly refused readings; the higher refusal rate is intended because it moves the existing admission email refusal earlier and adds no new rule.
criteria_check.evidence: The scan calls the existing `disallowed_emails` with the same `jc.config.personal_data`, so there is no second rule or allow-list. The allow-listed-address test shows it does not over-refuse. The persists test shows the refusal now happens at the producer stage with a line number. The 5% figure is the brief's estimate; I measured nothing (records/ is absent).

open_issues: records/ is absent, so I could not read introspection 20261025-074235-4nff or the outcomes of jobs 9e8t and akwq. Which condition produced the empty earlier_cases is unproven. The fix covers: a different class or category, five or more newer cases in the bucket, and a missing job_reasons source. If those two jobs were never introspected, new_class=true was correct for 4nff; the new flag now makes that repeat visible.
A run that fails in the producer loop builds no candidate, so a retry starts from the base, as an admission-refused job does today. No seed work was done.
A retry of a resumed job (the resume branch in run/mod.rs) does not re-run the scan, because that work already went through the producer loop. Admission still checks it.
Plan departures: the plan's step 8 and 9 and the Event/Records field names were followed. I did not edit docs/system-facts.md. Nothing else departed from the plan.
mistakes: I ran the full `cargo test --locked` once, but its output was too large and was saved outside the working directory, where the hook denied my reading it. I do not know the whole-workspace result and fell back to per-crate runs.
learnings: Admission details are '<path> <rule words>' strings built in admission.rs. The owner-maintained rule text itself contains '; ', so a split on '; ' needs a stem that stops before it. refusal_keys uses "is the owner's own document".

Introspection reads cases and classes from disk with read_records(self.git.dir()). It loads jobs and interventions from git with GitRecords::load. The two sources can disagree after the records cutover, so only job_reasons is overlaid from git.
Snapshot::work_tree_tree and Snapshot::git().run_bytes give a diff of the producer's work tree without building a candidate.

The policy hook denies reading Bash tool-result files saved outside the working directory, so a large `cargo test` output cannot be inspected afterwards. Use `-q` or a per-crate run when the output matters.
The producer.md line adds well under the 146-token headroom. The budgets test (system_facts_budgets_match_computed) still passes with docs/system-facts.md unedited.
desires: A way to read a saved large tool output inside the working directory, or a `cargo test` summary-only mode that Bash may use for the full suite.
